title: Hinton following Tatum at the Three Deuces
summary: Hinton recalls closing Tatum's fast numbers with Zutty Singleton's quartet in Chicago, unable to follow his changes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Oh, I agree. I remember working with Everett Barksdale with Zutty Singleton with the Three Deuces, and Lee Collins and Cozy Cole's brother was a piano player.

Yeah, and we worked at the Three Deuces in Zutty Singleton's band, quartet, and Art Tatum was a relief piano player, he played alone, but I had to come on for his finale, I had to come on because he played a fast tune, I had to come on and close him and take him off, see.

And he would go through these changes which I never caught. I had no way in the world of knowing where he was going, and I stood there like I was lost, and it was just amazing how far ahead of the times he was.
That was at least 1935 when I joined Cab Calloway's band.
